audits.title: A model for increasing patient safety in the intensive care unit: increasing the implementation rates of proven safety measures.
audits.standard: Evidence-based prophylaxis against venous thromboembolism, ventilator-associated pneumonia and stress ulcers
audits.setting: Intensive Care Unit, Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center

cycle1.result: Baseline implementation rates measured per patient-shift (values not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: Systematic approach to delivering safety measures, team communication tools, daily prompts in the ICU progress note and a data wall for real-time feedback.

cycle2.result: Mean implementation rose for each measure, with reduced variation and narrower control limits.

audits.other_findings: Control data also collected at an interim time point; success defined by both appropriate delivery and appropriate withholding.
audits.citation: Krimsky WS, Mroz IB, McIlwaine JK, Surgenor SD, Christian D, Corwin HL, et al.. A model for increasing patient safety in the intensive care unit: increasing the implementation rates of proven safety measures. Qual Saf Health Care. 2009;18(1):74-80. doi:10.1136/qshc.2007.024844. PMID: 19204137.

audits.title: Designing Technology to Decrease Pneumonia in Intubated Trauma Patients.
audits.standard: Chlorhexidine gluconate mouth care within 2 hours in ventilator bundle
audits.setting: Adult trauma intensive care unit, Deaconess Hospital, Evansville, Indiana
audits.intervention: Staff education on a redesigned electronic medical record ventilator bundle and chlorhexidine timing practice change

cycle2.result: 2-hour chlorhexidine documentation 73.3%; pneumonia in intubated patients decreased by 62%

audits.citation: Swearer JN, Hammer CL, Matthews SM, Meunier JL, Medler KL, Kamer GS, et al.. Designing Technology to Decrease Pneumonia in Intubated Trauma Patients. J Trauma Nurs. 2015;22(5):282-289. doi:10.1097/jtn.0000000000000155. PMID: 26352660.

audits.title: Audit of UK ventilator care bundles and discussion of subglottic secretion drainage.
audits.standard: Department of Health (2012) ventilator care bundle high impact intervention
audits.setting: UK intensive care units (national surveys of nurse leads and ICS linkmen)

cycle1.result: Over 95% worked in units using a ventilator bundle; compliance with each component exceeded 85% except subglottic secretion drainage (47-53% of units).

audits.other_findings: Lack of suitable endotracheal tubes meant some patients were re-intubated to allow subglottic secretion drainage; second survey had 77 responses.
audits.citation: Baldwin F, Gray R, Chequers M, Dyos J. Audit of UK ventilator care bundles and discussion of subglottic secretion drainage. Nurs Crit Care. 2016;21(5):265-270. doi:10.1111/nicc.12146. PMID: 27531399.

audits.title: Nurses' compliance to ventilator-associated pneumonia prevention bundle and its effect on patient outcomes in intensive care units.
audits.setting: ICUs of two tertiary hospitals, Muscat

cycle1.result: Nurses' compliance with VAP guidelines 69%, decreasing over the admission; 22.3% developed VAP (5.6 per 1000 ventilator days).

audits.other_findings: Better bundle compliance was linked to shorter length of stay.
audits.citation: Al-Harthi F, Al-Noumani H, Matua GA, Al-Abri H, Joseph A. Nurses' compliance to ventilator-associated pneumonia prevention bundle and its effect on patient outcomes in intensive care units. Nurs Crit Care. 2025;30(3):e70043. doi:10.1111/nicc.70043. PMID: 40276934.

audits.title: Striving for excellence in ventilator bundle compliance through continuous quality improvement initiative in the intensive care unit of a tertiary care hospital in India.
audits.standard: Ventilator bundle compliance (all five components documented); aim >90% within 6 months
audits.setting: 15-bed closed adult ICU, tertiary care hospital (Dr. S.N. Medical College, Jodhpur)

cycle1.result: Ventilator bundle compliance 40.7%, lowest for daily sedation vacation with SBT and thromboprophylaxis; VAP 62.4 per 1,000 ventilator days.

audits.intervention: PDSA cycles: multidisciplinary educational boot camp with WhatsApp group; bundle checklist in ICU progress chart signed by nurses and residents and countersigned by consultants, random inspections and a placard; simulation and micro-scenarios to standardise technique, with coloured bed marks for head elevation.

cycle2.period: September 2022 to August 2023 (6 months after compliance >90%)
cycle2.result: Compliance >70% after cycle 1 and >90% after cycle 2; VAP fell to 25.7 per 1,000 ventilator days (P=0.004; incidence rate ratio 2.34).

audits.other_findings: Total ventilation days and ICU length of stay also fell significantly (P=0.007 and P=0.002).
audits.citation: Paliwal N, Bihani P, Jaju R, Mohammed S, Prakash P, Tharu V. Striving for excellence in ventilator bundle compliance through continuous quality improvement initiative in the intensive care unit of a tertiary care hospital in India. Acute Crit Care. 2024;39(4):535-544. doi:10.4266/acc.2024.00101. PMID: 39558598.
